what: The bottom 167px strip of the screen becomes prism glass. The top of the strip is clear, and further down (1-t^2.3) the text and photos passing by look pulled down from above, with the R, G and B channels pushed separately at strengths 141, 149 and 157 so they split into a rainbow (Chromium backdrop-filter url). Other browsers get the same strip as an 8px blur plus a veil that darkens from the 60% point. Presses pass through downward

options.scales: R·G·B shift strength (three comma-separated values), default 141,149,157 — larger means a wider rainbow
options.curve: Bend that grows stronger toward the bottom (exponent), default 2.3
options.blur: Blur (px) for browsers that can’t refract, default 8
options.--fx-height: Band height when using CSS only, default 167px

note: The band sticks to the bottom of the screen with position: fixed. When attaching it to an inner panel (data-fx-scroller), give it position: absolute from the consuming css. backdrop-filter url() renders only in Chromium, so Safari and Product get a plain blur band (same as the original).
